fields.meta_description: Build an employee engagement survey with anonymous team results, eNPS, driver analysis and manager action plans. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build an Employee Engagement Survey From Question to Action
fields.hero_description: Describe your teams and what you need to learn. Emergent builds the questions, anonymous team results, driver analysis and manager dashboards, in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What an Engagement Survey Needs to Work
fields.features_subheading: An employee engagement survey measures how committed people are to their work and employer, and what drives that number.
fields.feature_1:
Questions grouped by engagement driver

Core items on pride, intent to stay, advocacy and extra effort come first. Driver sections on managers, growth, recognition and workload follow. Reword any item with one sentence.
fields.feature_2:
Anonymity thresholds you set

Results stay hidden for any group with fewer than five answers, and comments show no names or emails. The first screen states that rule before anyone answers a question.
fields.feature_3:
Engagement index and eNPS per team

Each team gets an engagement index from the core items and an eNPS from one 0-10 question, shown next to the company result and the team's own score from the last cycle.
fields.feature_4:
Driver analysis that ranks what to fix

Each team's driver scores are correlated with its engagement index. The items that move it most rise to the top of the manager's view, ahead of the averages for all 40 questions.
fields.feature_5:
Org data synced from your HRIS

Department, location, tenure and manager sync from your HRIS, such as BambooHR or Workday. Results split along those lines without a single demographic question in the survey.
fields.feature_6:
Action plans the next survey checks

Managers log the actions they agreed with their team after each cycle. The next survey asks whether each one landed, and the answers appear beside the action they refer to.

fields.usecase_heading: Engagement Surveys to Build This Week
fields.tab_content_1:
A yearly census that names each team's focus driver

A 40-question survey goes to all 600 employees for two weeks, with reminders only to people who have not answered. Teams with fewer than five answers stay hidden but still count in the totals. Each manager sees their team's index and eNPS beside the driver that moves it most, then logs actions.
fields.tab_content_2:
Frontline staff answer on a phone in two minutes

Store and warehouse staff without a company email scan a QR code in the break room and answer 12 questions in English or Spanish. The code tags each response to its site, and results stay hidden from the site manager until that site has five answers.
fields.tab_content_3:
Find the teams a reorg has unsettled

Six weeks after a reorg, affected teams answer a short survey on role clarity and trust in leadership, plus the core intent-to-stay item. Each team's intent to stay is compared with its last census, and a drop of 10 points or more alerts the HR business partner in Slack.
fields.tab_content_4:
Track eNPS every quarter without survey fatigue

Each quarter, people answer the 0-10 recommend question and one open question on what would raise their score. A live dashboard tracks the company eNPS quarter over quarter. In Q3 the score rose from +12 to +18, and 400 comments fell into four themes led by growth.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Engagement Survey
fields.howto_description: An engagement survey is worth what managers do with its results. These steps start with the decisions you want to make and end with the first action plan.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Decide what you will act on
fields.howto_step_1_des: Start with the decisions the results should inform, such as whether engineering attrition after a hiring freeze is a manager problem or a workload problem. Every question should map to one of them. Items nobody acts on teach people that answering changes nothing.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Use four to six core items for engagement itself and never reword them between cycles. A changed item breaks the comparison with last year. Add driver sections for the areas from step one, written as single statements on the same 1-5 agreement scale.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Set the smallest group whose results anyone can see. Five answers is the usual floor: a group with fewer stays hidden, while its answers still count in company totals. Take team and tenure from your HRIS. The survey itself should never ask for them.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Write it out in plain English: who gets it, which questions, the scale, the anonymity rule and the reminder schedule. Emergent turns that into a working survey with its own response table and team dashboards. Later changes take one more message.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell people why you are asking and the date results come back. Keep the survey open for two weeks and remind only those who have not answered. A live response rate by department shows managers where a nudge is needed.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Read the drivers, not the averages
fields.howto_step_6_des: Start with each team's two headline numbers, then the drivers most tied to them. A low item that does not move engagement can wait. A middling one that does is where the first action belongs.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Share company and team results within a month. Each manager then agrees a short list of actions with their team and logs it on the dashboard. People keep answering when the next survey asks about those actions by name.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build an Employee Engagement Survey From Question to Action', title 'Employee Engagement Survey You Can Act On' and hero ('the questions, anonymous team results, driver analysis and manager dashboards') cover the whole job; no sibling topic.

intent.evidence: Top 10 is Gallup Q12, question lists (Culture Amp, DecisionWise), a SurveyMonkey template and vendor directories (SHRM, Perceptyx); the page gives ten example items (FAQ 5), a template answer (FAQ 14), a vendor table and FAQ 12, a 7-step how-to, and all 9 PAA questions.

specificity.evidence: Buyer vocabulary throughout ('engagement index', 'eNPS', 'focus driver', 'HR business partner', 'BambooHR or Workday'); table uses the employee variant 'Pulse and annual surveys, anonymous reporting, and manager dashboards, as code you own'.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence that says what happens, e.g. feature_6 'Managers log the actions they agreed with their team after each cycle.'; FAQ 13 'Not exactly.' and FAQ 14 'Yes.' answer directly.

craft.evidence: The cycle-2 'which is what keeps people answering' construction is back in a new spot: faq 1 'The core items stay the same each cycle, and that is what lets a team read this year's score against last year's.' (defect #4, tacked-on clause; end on the point, e.g. 'Keeping the core items fixed each cycle makes this year's score comparable with last year's.'). Also howto_step_3_des '...a group with fewer stays hidden, while its answers still count in company totals' trails a second idea onto the rule; split it. All seven cycle-2 ', so' tails and both which-clauses are otherwise fixed; 'two or three' now appears once (faq 4).

voice.evidence: One phrase used three times, the recycled-phrase pattern cycle 2 failed: tab_content_1 'stay hidden but still count in the totals', howto_step_3_des 'stays hidden, while its answers still count in company totals', faq 10 'Legal's three answers stay hidden but still count in the totals'. Keep it once (tab 1) and cut or reword the other two. Same pattern, smaller: howto_step_4_des 'a working survey with its own response table and team dashboards' returns as faq 14 'it arrives with its response table and dashboards already connected' (cycle 2 flagged this pair in step 4 / faq 2).

truth.evidence: faq 10 now frames the census as the page's own example ('The census in the first tab is a worked example'), no longer a 'typical' norm; index (118x76+84x69+66x58+141x77)/409 = 72.0 and eNPS +15.8 to +16.5 give '72 out of 100' and '+16'; Engineering 118 and Operations 141 are the two largest and both show Growth; Platform 81 to 67 = -14; 142+118+86+54 = 400; one anonymity rule, 'fewer than five answers', everywhere; FAQ 12 vendor pricing matches the library table.

distinct.evidence: Own territory per the watch-list (commitment and eNPS drivers): census, frontline QR, post-reorg and quarterly eNPS scenes share nothing with /customer-satisfaction; satisfaction and pulse are handed off by link in faq 13 and 15.

faq.evidence: 15 real questions, each answered in its first sentence, but answers still repeat the body (cycle 2 required each to add something new): faq 1 'The core items stay the same each cycle, and that is what lets a team read this year's score against last year's' restates howto_step_2 'never reword them between cycles. A changed item breaks the comparison with last year'; faq 10's last sentence 'Legal's three answers stay hidden but still count in the totals' repeats tab_content_1 'stay hidden but still count in the totals' nearly word for word; faq 14 'response table and dashboards already connected' repeats step 4. Replace each with a fact the body lacks. P2: faq 10 'a worked example' is the wrong term (no working is shown); say 'an example'.

images.evidence: New cover and share card 'Q3 eNPS check-in' / 'eNPS, up from +12 in Q2' / '+18' / '0-10 question plus one comment' reads full with no empty band and agrees with tab 4 '+18, Q3, up from +12' and tab 4 copy 'one open question'; uc-1 412 of 600 = 118+84+66+141+3, Legal 'Hidden, under 5 answers'; uc-2 Store 214 '5 answered' unlocked; uc-3 Platform -14 against a 10-point rule; uc-4 400 comments in four themes led by Growth 142.
